analysis: Only docs changed: docs/architecture/inference.md head 1030-1047 adds a description of the PromptTokenCache and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites prompt-preparation path. All other lines in units :10 and :11 are unchanged context; I examined them for reference only. Claimed controls: IDs equal the unchanged applyChatTemplate output; there is a load-time comparison plus sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on mismatch; reuse never crosses a cache scope; DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 rolls back. Source for PromptTokenCache.swift, LocalTokenizerBridge and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites was not supplied, so none of these claims can be verified. Integration should check four things. (1) The scope key is the coordinator-authored cacheSalt (T-041 mitigation), not prompt_cache_key or user. (2) The cache's retention bounds and eviction on unload or logout. (3) Whether the linear-time template rewrites could diverge from the served template before a sampled check catches it; divergence would affect prompt-contract and cache identity, with T-007-like integrity impact. (4) Whether parallel encoding on four cores adds a DoS lever for long prompts. One low finding records the threat-model gap; it is not proven to be an exploit.

findings.detail: Head lines 1030-1046 document a new `PromptTokenCache` that keeps token IDs of rendered prompt pieces and reuses them for later requests in the same prefix-cache scope. Those cached pieces are derived from consumer prompts (A-001). T-041 covers only the encrypted SSD KV tier and its TTL, disk budget and KEK purge. T-028 covers residual GPU/KV memory. Neither covers this host-RAM cache. The doc gives no retention bound (TTL, size or eviction) and no purge on unload or logout. Reuse also shortens tokenization time for a repeated piece, which adds a second hit/miss latency signal. That signal would fall within the SEC-035 same-scope oracle only if scoping really uses the coordinator-authored cacheSalt rather than a caller field. Trigger: a same-scope co-tenant probes guessed history pieces, or an operator inspects process memory (ADV-001, T-014). Fix: record this cache in T-041/T-028 with its scope source, size/TTL bounds and purge points. Confirm the scope key comes from the coordinator and that `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0` disables it.
findings.title: New in-memory PromptTokenCache retains prompt-derived token IDs without threat-model coverage
